newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil minister says pay ruling will be passed on.
newsitem.headline: Brazil minister says pay ruling will be passed on.

text.p: A 28.9 percent pay rise awarded to 11 Brazilian civil servants will inevitably be passed on to the rest of the federal government's workforce, Brazil's Social Security Minister said.
"The decision for the 11 is a decision for everyone," Reinhold Stephanes told Reuters after the Supreme Federal Tribunal ruled in favor of the civil servants claim.
The minister said the government would not be able to prevent the rest of the federal goverment workforce, which totals about 540,000 employees, from taking out similar suits.
Stephanes compared the situation to a ruling in 1991 when a trade union won a case involving social security payments. That verdict was then extended to members of other unions.

"This is going to mean no more (new) pay raises for the next few years," the minister said. The government would also probably seek to soften the blow of any massive payout to federal workers by divvying up the outlay into instalments.
Stephanes said the ruling showed how vulnerable the government was to court decisions, principally because so many issues relating to pay and benefits are enshrined in Brazil's constitution.
"The problem is that lots of economic decisions that should be resolved within the government end up being judged in the courts," he said.

Administration Minister Luiz Carlos Bresser Pereira, who is responsible for the civil service and recently said an STF ruling in favor of the 11 workers would be "a national disaster", declined to speak with reporters.
